title: Consistent session snapshots for async stream metering
creator: Marco Ruiz
description:
Problem: Async streaming sessions (long-lived websockets, resumed streams, and multiplexed client connections) produce fragmented token events across multiple micro-batches. Due to out-of-order delivery, retries, mid-stream model switches, and partial resume semantics we currently see transient mismatches between the live aggregator totals and the authoritative runtime intent. These mismatches lead to over/under-billing, quota miscounts, and noisy alerts for high-throughput customers.

Observed failure modes: duplicate fragment emission on retry, partial finalization when client disconnects mid-response, midstream model fallback emitting both variant tokens, and resumed sessions producing overlapping prefix attributions. Existing dedupe heuristics (fragment id + window) fail when fragments are retried with new ids or when fragments are split at different boundaries by gateways.

Goal: Implement a lightweight, deterministic session snapshot mechanism that the serving runtime emits at well-defined commit points (session end, model switch, periodic checkpoint). The metering ingestion pipeline will consume snapshots as authoritative reconciliation anchors and perform a correction pass to align aggregator state with runtime snapshots. This should preserve streaming low-latency metering, add bounded reconciliation latency (configurable), and avoid retroactive charges visible to customers except when corrections exceed a small threshold.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change tokenization logic across runtimes or change pricing; it focuses on accounting correctness and alignment between runtime and ledger aggregates.
suggested_approach: 1) Runtime: add optional 'session_snapshot' event with deterministic fields {session_id, seq, total_input_tokens, total_output_tokens, model_variant, timestamp, fingerprint}. Emit at session end, on model switch, and at periodic heartbeat (default 30s). 2) Ingestion: accept session_snapshot events and route to reconciliation topic. 3) Aggregator: add reconciliation stage that compares live aggregates to snapshot; produce correction records (credit/debit) with provenance. 4) Backfill: run reconciliation job for last 7 days for high-usage customers. 5) Feature flag the reconciliation pass and incremental rollout for top 10 customers. 6) Add e2e tests for resume/idempotency/partial-finalize scenarios.
risk_assessment: Medium-high: touches critical billing path. Risks include double-correction, race conditions between snapshot and in-flight fragments, and increased traffic to aggregation services. Mitigations: feature flag rollout, snapshot tombstone semantics (apply snapshot only once per seq), idempotent correction records, and throttled reconciliation workers.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits session_snapshot events for end/resume/model-switch/heartbeat in staging
Aggregator applies snapshot reconciliation deterministically and produces correction records visible in billing ledger
End-to-end tests demonstrate reconciliation converges within 2 minutes for simulated interleaved fragments
No net increase in duplicate charges observed for canary customers (<=0.01% differential) during rollout
Console dashboards updated: 'snapshot_reconciliations' metric, per-session corrections, and alerts for corrections > 1% of session cost
comments: 2026-02-18 Marco Ruiz: Triage - assigned to Aisha. Captured customer reports (cust-42) where resumed sessions billed double for last chunk.

2026-02-20 Aisha Patel: Spike completed. Implemented runtime prototype that emits snapshot with fingerprint = sha256(prefix_tokens || last_seq). Observed that gateway splitting causes seq renumbering; need stable session ids across proxies.

2026-02-24 Loren Kim (Arch review): Prefer a small structured snapshot rather than full fragment replay. Keep snapshot size under 1KB. Ensure HMACed fingerprint to prevent tampering for private deployments.
2026-02-26 QA: e2e harness shows reconciliation corrects undercounts for resumed stream but leaves rare duplicates when retries occur within 200ms. Proposed short debounce window at ingestion.

2026-03-01 PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/462 - adds snapshot consumer and correction record schema. Needs tests for idempotency and a migration plan for existing aggregator state.
2026-03-02 PM review (Evan Brooks): Prioritize canary rollout for top 5 customers; add customer communication template for visible corrections over 0.5%.

2026-03-02 Aisha Patel: Updated implementation plan to include tombstone semantics: apply snapshot only if seq > last_applied_seq for session_id. Added backlog ticket for cross-region snapshot relay (ENG-55890).
